original_source_text: Logic Equivalence Checking (LEC) is often bottlenecked by synthesis-induced structural perturbations and XOR-dense regions that hinder SAT solving. We contend that the *modeling* of the miter is as critical as the SAT solver itself and propose a miter-aware mapping framework that reformulates the problem before solving by constructing a LUT-based miter preserving structural correspondence and exposing high-level logic relations. It integrates equivalence-preserving mapping, Gaussian-guided XOR modeling, and solver-oriented LUT selection to produce solver-efficient representations. Experiments on comprehensive benchmarks show up to 92.1% reduction across state-of-the-art SAT solvers, highlighting the importance of solver-aware modeling in enhancing LEC efficiency.
